title: What's your favourite kind of noodle?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: change or alter something in a creative way to make something new and exciting
unusual and exciting because of coming from far away
at some unspecified time in the past
change or alter something slightly to improve it
(idiom) do things which challenge normal acceptable behaviour

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，这里是BBC学英语的6 Minute English节目。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. Do you enjoy eating noodles, Beth?
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔。我是贝丝。贝丝，你喜欢吃面条吗？

sentences.en: I love noodles, yes. I think my favourite are udon – the big thick ones.
sentences.zh: 我挺喜欢面条的。我想我最喜欢乌冬面——那种又粗又劲道的面。

sentences.en: Mmm, they're so good! Well, some people buy them dried in a packet, others make them fresh from wheat or rice, but there is little doubt that noodles are popular around the world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们太好吃了！有的人买包装好的干面，有的人用小麦或大米现做，毫无疑问，面条在世界各地都非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: From their origins, probably somewhere in China, noodle recipes were spread by traders on the ancient Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 从它们的起源来看——可能在中国的某个地方，面条的制作方法是通过古代丝绸之路上的商人们传播开来的。

sentences.en: At each destination along the road, people gave noodles a twist, adding different flavours and ingredients to create a new dish.
sentences.zh: 沿着丝绸之路的每一个目的地，人们都对面条进行了改良，加入不同的风味和食材，创造出一种全新的菜肴。

sentences.en: In this programme, we'll visit the United States and Japan, two countries which have taken noodles and created exciting new varieties.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将前往美国和日本，这两个国家将面条发扬光大，创造出了令人兴奋的新品种。

sentences.en: As usual, we'll learn some useful new vocabulary, and remember – you can read along with the transcript of this programme, available now on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 像往常一样，我们将学习一些实用的新词汇，记住——你可以边听边读本节目的文稿，现在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上就可以查看。

sentences.en: But first, Neil, I have a question for you.
sentences.zh: 但首先，尼尔，我有一个问题要问你。

sentences.en: As well as different shapes and ingredients, noodles come in many different flavours.
sentences.zh: 除了不同的形状和食材，面条还有各种各样的风味。

sentences.en: So which region of China is famous for its spicy flavours?
sentences.zh: 那么中国哪个地区以麻辣风味闻名呢？

sentences.en: Is it: a) Shanghai, b) Sichuan, or c) Guangzhou?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 上海，b) 四川，还是 c) 广州？

sentences.en: Well, I think actually, Beth, I know the answer to this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实我觉得，贝丝，我知道答案。

sentences.en: I've been lucky enough to have been to this place.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运曾去过这个地方。

sentences.en: I think it's b) Sichuan. OK. Well, you sound confident.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是 b) 四川。好吧。听起来你很有信心。

sentences.en: I will reveal the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 我会在节目稍后揭晓答案。

sentences.en: BBC World Service programme, The Food Chain, investigated how noodles spread from Asia through Europe to America.
sentences.zh: BBC世界服务部的节目《The Food Chain》探讨了面条是如何从亚洲经欧洲传到美洲的。

sentences.en: They uncovered a surprising story: that pasta comes from noodles brought back to Italy by Marco Polo in the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 他们揭开了一个令人惊奇的故事：意大利面其实源自马可·波罗在13世纪从中国带回意大利的面条。

sentences.en: Jen Lin-Liu, author of the book 'On the Noodle Road', doesn't believe this story.
sentences.zh: 《面条之路》一书的作者珍·林-刘并不相信这个说法。

sentences.en: So, noodles were very exotic in the 1920s and 30s in the United States, and there was a new pasta association in America that wanted to promote the manufacturing of dried pasta.
sentences.zh: 所以，在20世纪20和30年代的美国，面条是非常有异国情调的，当时美国有一个新的意面协会，想要推广干意面的生产。

sentences.en: And so they came up with a story about how Marco Polo went to China and found the noodle there, and brought it all the way to Italy.
sentences.zh: 于是他们编造了一个故事，讲马可·波罗如何去了中国并发现了面条，然后一路把它带到了意大利。

sentences.en: In the 1920s, noodles were popular because they were exotic, meaning foreign, unusual and exciting.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪20年代，面条很受欢迎，因为它们很“异国情调”，意思是来自外国、不同寻常且令人兴奋。

sentences.en: At that time pasta companies were promoting a new invention, dried pasta, so they came up with a story about Marco Polo to sell more pasta.
sentences.zh: 当时意面公司正在推广一项新发明——干意面，所以他们编造了关于马可·波罗的故事来卖出更多的意面。

sentences.en: If you come up with something, you suggest or think up an idea.
sentences.zh: 如果你 come up with（想出、提出）某事，你就是提出或构思了一个主意。

sentences.en: And it worked – sales of pasta jumped as a result!
sentences.zh: 这招管用了——结果意面的销量猛增！

sentences.en: Now, our second destination, Japan, also has a history of eating noodles.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们的第二个目的地日本，也有吃面的历史。

sentences.en: One of the most famous Japanese noodle dishes is ramen, and Frank Striegl, a blogger living in Tokyo, knows all about it.
sentences.zh: 最有名的日本面食之一就是拉面，住在东京的博主弗兰克·斯特里格尔对它了如指掌。

sentences.en: He eats over 300 bowls of ramen a year! He explained to BBC World Service's The Food Chain how Chinese immigrants to Japan in the late 1800s influenced this Japanese dish.
sentences.zh: 他一年要吃300多碗拉面！他向BBC世界服务部的《The Food Chain》解释了19世纪末移居日本的中国移民是如何影响这种日本美食的。

sentences.en: And at one point or another, different chefs decided to localise these dishes.
sentences.zh: 在过去的某个时候，不同的厨师决定将这些菜肴本地化。

sentences.en: They said, "We love these Chinese noodle dishes.
sentences.zh: 他们说：“我们喜欢这些中国的面条。”

sentences.en: However, why don't we tweak them? Why don't we make them a little bit more Japanese?"
sentences.zh: “然而，我们为什么不稍微改良一下呢？为什么不让它们更日本化一点呢？”

sentences.en: Frank says that at one point or another, chefs started to make noodle dishes more Japanese.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克说，在过去的某个时间点，厨师们开始让面条料理变得更具日本特色。

sentences.en: Here, the phrase at one point or another means at some unspecified time in the past.
sentences.zh: 这里，短语 at one point or another 的意思是过去某个不确定的时间。

sentences.en: They did this by tweaking Chinese noodles – in other words, by changing them slightly to make them better, different or, in this case, more Japanese.
sentences.zh: 他们通过微调中国面条来做到这一点——换句话说，就是稍微改变它们，让它们更好、与众不同，或者在这种情况下，更具日本特色。

sentences.en: By making these tweaks, adding new toppings and slices of beef or chicken, Japanese chefs created the noodle dish we know today as ramen.
sentences.zh: 通过这些调整，加入新的配料以及牛肉或鸡肉片，日本厨师创造了我们今天所知道的拉面。

sentences.en: Here's Frank Striegl again, talking with BBC World Service's The Food Chain.
sentences.zh: 再次听听弗兰克·斯特里格尔与BBC世界服务部《The Food Chain》的对话。

sentences.en: And what I find fascinating about ramen, compared to perhaps other wonderful noodle dishes around the world, is that ramen continues to evolve.
sentences.zh: 我觉得拉面最迷人的地方在于，与世界上其他美妙的面条相比，拉面一直在不断演变。

sentences.en: Unlike other Japanese foods, it's OK to push the boundaries.
sentences.zh: 不像其他日本食物，打破常规（推陈出新）是完全可以接受的。

sentences.en: Frank thinks that Japanese ramen continues to evolve – to develop and change gradually in response to new developments and ideas.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克认为日本拉面一直在不断演变——为了应对新的发展和理念而逐渐发展和改变。

sentences.en: Unlike other traditional food such as sushi, modern versions of ramen push the boundaries.
sentences.zh: 不像寿司等其他传统食物，现代版本的拉面在不断突破极限。

sentences.en: If you push the boundaries, you act in a way which challenges normal acceptable behaviour.
sentences.zh: 如果你 push the boundaries（突破常规 / 挑战极限），你的行为就会挑战正常的可接受行为。

sentences.en: Yes, noodles have changed so much since ancient times that today you can buy them dried in a packet and simply add hot water.
sentences.zh: 是的，面条自古以来已经发生了巨大的变化，以至于今天你可以买到一包干面条，然后直接加热水冲泡。

sentences.en: But the flavours and the noodles themselves maintain a link to the past.
sentences.zh: 但风味和面条本身依然保持着与过去的联系。

sentences.en: Now, speaking of flavours, what was the answer to your question, Beth?
sentences.zh: 说到风味，你问题的答案是什么，贝丝？

sentences.en: Well, I asked you which region of China is famous for its spicy flavours.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我问你中国哪个地区以麻辣风味闻名。

sentences.en: You were very confident with saying Sichuan and that is the correct answer.
sentences.zh: 你非常自信地说是四川，这正是正确答案。

sentences.en: Sichuan is a place that is famous for spicy food, such as the Sichuan pepper and Sichuan hotpot.
sentences.zh: 四川是一个以辛辣食物闻名的地方，比如四川花椒和四川火锅。

sentences.en: OK. It's time to recap the vocabulary we've learnt.
sentences.zh: 好的。是时候回顾我们学过的词汇了。

sentences.en: If you give something a twist, you change it in some small way to create something new and exciting.
sentences.zh: 如果你给某事 give a twist（赋予新意 / 作出改变），你就会在某些小地方对其进行改变，以创造出新奇有趣的东西。

sentences.en: The adjective exotic means unusual and exciting because of coming from far away.
sentences.zh: 形容词 exotic（异国情调的）意指由于来自远方而不同寻常且令人兴奋。

sentences.en: The phrase, at one point or another means at some unspecified time in the past.
sentences.zh: 短语 at one point or another（不知何时 / 曾几何时）意指过去某个不确定的时间。

sentences.en: If you tweak something, you alter it slightly in order to improve it.
sentences.zh: 如果你 tweak（微调）某物，你就会对其进行轻微的改动以便改进它。

sentences.en: Something which evolves, develops and changes gradually.
sentences.zh: 演变的事物（something which evolves），是指在逐渐发展和改变。

sentences.en: And finally, the idiom to push the boundaries means to do things which challenge normal acceptable behaviour.
sentences.zh: 最后，习语 push the boundaries（突破极限 / 挑战常规）意指去做那些挑战正常可接受行为的事。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. If you enjoyed the programme, why not visit our website and check out all of the different podcasts that we have at BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟节目时间又到了。如果你喜欢这个节目，为什么不去我们的网站看看我们在 BBC Learning English 上提供的各种播客呢？

sentences.en: There's something there for everyone. Thanks for joining us and goodbye.
sentences.zh: 总有一款适合你。感谢收听，再见。

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
